dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats exactly at the star’s own brightness-variation period measured by TESS (0.78 d, ~13000 ppm), with a huge out-of-eclipse swing and changing depth that a planet cannot explain. The star is flagged by Gaia as an astrometric binary. Together this is a stellar binary/pulsation alias, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Very high RUWE indicates Gaia astrometry inconsistent with single star, supporting EB/binary scenario with xgboost planet_rank 0.12.
Large out-of-eclipse swing (655.8 ppm, chi2 98.67 dof 7) is 38% of transit depth, expected for ellipsoidal/beaming of close binary, not planet.

Depth changes dramatically and sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source even within QLP (310 vs 852 ppm), inconsistent with a stable planet; centroid on_target (1.119 arcsec, 0.8365 sigma) rules out NEB.
Dip period is 1/(2/3) of true 0.781 d rotation period measured with amplitude 12793 and 12951 ppm; the signal is stellar variability/pulsation at the rotation alias, not a transit.
reasons.value: rotation_d 0.5855 vs period 0.78 (signal_over_rotation 1.333), sector 6/7 period 0.781 d false_alarm 7.633e-297

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed shape and 0.78 d period are consistent with evolved K dwarf (Teff 4350 K, rad 0.7086) binary/pulsations, not a planet; secondary snr -14.78 and low xgboost rank disfavour planet despite size 3.192 Rearth.
reasons.value: duration ratio 1.471, fit_b 0.02446, v_sigma -5.261 but star_density_penalty 6611
